case_studies.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
case_studies.abstract: Existing agent benchmarks typically evaluate agents on well-specified tasks defined by issue reports, specifications, or task tickets. Real-world customer delivery is different: forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) must clarify ambiguous requirements, work in live systems, and uncover unstated constraints. We introduce FDE-Gym, a benchmark of 95 end-to-end delivery tasks from 20 customer scenarios across 18 sectors, each adapted by industry experts from real-world delivery projects. case_studies.summary: This study tackles the gap in AI agent testing by creating FDE-Gym, a realistic benchmark of 95 delivery tasks that mirror real‑world engineering challenges such as ambiguous requirements and live system constraints. The authors built a simulated environment with scripted stakeholders and editable customer systems, allowing agents to practice end‑to‑end delivery. The result is a more industry‑relevant testing suite that better reflects the complexity of actual IT projects.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work
case_studies.score_reasoning: The benchmark focuses on real‑world delivery tasks that mirror the ambiguity and live‑system constraints IT engineers face, providing insights that could inform tool development and training. It is directly relevant to engineers working with SaaS, cloud, and automation platforms. While the research offers actionable ideas, most applications would require some engineering effort, yielding a moderate 90‑day value.

case_studies.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
case_studies.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents and multi-agent systems increasingly tackle complex tasks through long-horizon tool use and inter-agent collaboration. However, these systems are prone to deviating from the overall goal as execution unfolds, which wastes execution resources and leads to undesired outcomes, a failure termed goal drift. In this work, we propose a steering agent that supervises execution on the fly and steers the system back on track when drift occurs. case_studies.summary: Goal drift causes LLM agents and multi‑agent systems to wander off target, wasting resources and producing bad outcomes. The authors built a steering agent that watches execution in real time and nudges the system back on track with quick, low‑cost interventions. The result is a more reliable, efficient system that stays aligned with its objectives.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage LLM‑powered workflows, add a steering layer: 1) monitor agent outputs for deviation signals, 2) trigger a lightweight correction routine when drift is detected, 3) log interventions for future tuning.
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper introduces a steering agent to mitigate goal drift in LLM-powered agents, a concept that could inform the design of agent-based automation for IT infrastructure. While the idea is novel and could inspire new tooling, its immediate applicability to existing Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, or cloud management workflows is limited. Practical steps for implementation are not detailed, and the benefit within a 90‑day horizon would likely be minimal.
